claim: A protein's genetic architecture determines its possible evolutionary trajectories.
source: A protein's genetic architecture – the set of causal rules by which its sequence produces its functions – also determines its possible evolutionary trajectories.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract establishing a relationship between genetic architecture and evolutionary trajectories.

claim: Prior research has proposed that the genetic architecture of proteins is very complex, with pervasive epistatic interactions that constrain evolution.
source: Prior research has proposed that the genetic architecture of proteins is very complex, with pervasive epistatic interactions that constrain evolution and make function difficult to predict from sequence.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research in the field.

claim: Most prior work on protein genetic architecture has analyzed only the direct paths between two proteins of interest, excluding the vast majority of possible genotypes and evolutionary trajectories.
source: Most of this work has analyzed only the direct paths between two proteins of interest – excluding the vast majority of possible genotypes and evolutionary trajectories
evidence: This is a characterization of limitations in prior research.

claim: The genetic architecture of DNA recognition in the studied transcription factor consists of a dense set of main and pairwise effects involving virtually every possible amino acid state in the protein-DNA interface.
source: We show that the genetic architecture of DNA recognition consists of a dense set of main and pairwise effects that involve virtually every possible amino acid state in the protein-DNA interface, but higher-order epistasis plays only a tiny role.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's analysis of the DMS data.

claim: Higher-order epistasis plays only a tiny role in the genetic architecture of DNA recognition in the studied transcription factor.
source: We show that the genetic architecture of DNA recognition consists of a dense set of main and pairwise effects that involve virtually every possible amino acid state in the protein-DNA interface, but higher-order epistasis plays only a tiny role.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's analysis.

claim: Pairwise interactions enlarge the set of functional sequences in the studied transcription factor.
source: Pairwise interactions enlarge the set of functional sequences and are the primary determinants of specificity for different DNA elements.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's analysis of the genetic architecture.

claim: Pairwise interactions are the primary determinants of specificity for different DNA elements in the studied transcription factor.
source: Pairwise interactions enlarge the set of functional sequences and are the primary determinants of specificity for different DNA elements.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's analysis.

claim: Pairwise epistasis massively expands the number of opportunities for single-residue mutations to switch specificity from one DNA target to another.
source: They also massively expand the number of opportunities for single-residue mutations to switch specificity from one DNA target to another.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's analysis of mutational opportunities.

claim: Pairwise epistasis facilitates rather than constrains the evolution of new functions by bringing variants with different functions close together in sequence space.
source: By bringing variants with different functions close together in sequence space, pairwise epistasis therefore facilitates rather than constrains the evolution of new functions.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion from the study's evolutionary simulations and sequence space analysis.

claim: Epistasis could constrain evolution by creating a rugged functional landscape in sequence space.
source: Epistasis could also constrain evolution by creating a rugged functional landscape in sequence space, in which many optimal or near-optimal genotypes are inaccessible from others under most evolutionary scenarios (Breen et al., 2012; Carneiro and Hartl, 2010; Chen and Conrad, 1994; Conrad, 1998; Domingo et al., 2019; Franke et al., 2011; Gavrilets, 1997; Gavrilets and Gravner, 1997; Goldstein et al., 2015; Kauffman and Weinberger, 1989; Kauffman and Levin, 1987; Kondrashov and Kondrashov, 2015; McCandlish et al., 2013; Miton et al., 2021; Payne and Wagner, 2019; Pollock et al., 2012; Romero and Arnold, 2009; Shah et al., 2015; Smith, 1970; Starr and Thornton, 2016; Usmanova et al., 2015; Whitlock et al., 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior theoretical and empirical work.

claim: Epistatic interactions can predominantly impair function through 'diminishing returns' of otherwise favorable mutations.
source: A related topic is potential bias in epistatic interactions: if they predominantly impair function, 'diminishing the returns' of otherwise favorable mutations (Chou et al., 2011; Cvijović et al., 2018; Johnson et al., 2019; Kryazhimskiy et al., 2014; Lyons et al., 2020; Reddy and Desai, 2021; Tokuriki et al., 2012; Wei and Zhang, 2019; Wünsche et al., 2017)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Epistasis is clearly present in the genetic architecture of proteins.
source: Epistasis is clearly present in the genetic architecture of proteins (Ashenberg et al., 2013; Bank et al., 2015; Bridgham et al., 2009; Bridgham et al., 2006; Ding et al., 2022; Emlaw et al., 2020; Faber et al., 2019; Gong et al., 2013; Gong and Bloom, 2014; Kumar et al., 2017; Lunzer et al., 2010; Ortlund et al., 2007; Park et al., 2022; Pokusaeva et al., 2019; Starr, 1979; Starr et al., 2018; Tufts et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2013)
evidence: This claim is supported by extensive citations to prior experimental work.

claim: Studies of pairs of mutations show that pairwise interactions can block some two-step paths near a designated wild-type protein.
source: Studies of pairs of mutations show that pairwise interactions can block some two-step paths near a designated wild-type protein (Adams et al., 2019; Diss and Lehner, 2018; Olson et al., 2014; Salinas and Ranganathan, 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Experiments on higher order combinations have found that epistasis can reduce the number of functional intermediates that connect a designated pair of starting and ending proteins.
source: experiments on higher order combinations have found that epistasis can reduce the number of functional intermediates that connect a designated pair of starting and ending proteins (Buda et al., 2022; de Visser and Krug, 2014; Jochumsen et al., 2016; Phillips et al., 2021; Sailer et al., 2020; Sailer and Harms, 2017a; Szendro et al., 2013; Weinreich et al., 2018; Weinreich et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Most combinatorial studies have assessed just two states per site, excluding most of the huge ensemble of potential genotypes and evolutionary paths.
source: Most combinatorial studies, however, have assessed just two states per site (Aakre et al., 2015; Anderson et al., 2021; Anderson et al., 2015; Bridgham et al., 2009; Bridgham et al., 2006; Brown et al., 2010; de Visser et al., 2009; Dutta et al., 2010; Field and Matz, 2010; Jenson et al., 2017; Jiang et al., 2013; Khan et al., 2011; Kumar et al., 2017; Lee et al., 1997; Lozovsky et al., 2009; Lunzer et al., 2005; Malcolm et al., 1990; Meini et al., 2015; Miton and Tokuriki, 2016; Moriuchi et al., 2014; Natarajan et al., 2013; Noor et al., 2012; O'Maille et al., 2008; Palmer et al., 2015; Poelwijk et al., 2019; Poelwijk et al., 2016; Reetz and Sanchis, 2008; Tufts et al., 2015; Weinreich et al., 2006; Yang et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2012), thus excluding most of the huge ensemble of potential genotypes and the evolutionary paths among them.
evidence: This is a characterization of limitations in prior research, supported by extensive citations.

claim: Most methods for dissecting genetic architecture from combinatorial studies have been limited to just two states per site.
source: Most methods for dissecting genetic architecture from combinatorial studies have been limited to just two states per site (but see Brookes et al., 2022; Faure et al., 2023a; Faure et al., 2023b; Park et al., 2023).
evidence: This is a characterization of methodological limitations in prior research, with citations.

claim: Most studies have modeled the effects of mutations relative to a particular wild-type reference sequence, which yields globally inaccurate estimates when mutations are introduced into other backgrounds.
source: Another concern is that most studies have modeled the effects of mutations relative to a particular wild-type reference sequence, which yields globally inaccurate estimates of the effects of mutations and combinations when they are introduced into other backgrounds (Poelwijk et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a characterization of a methodological limitation in prior research, supported by citation.

claim: Steroid hormone receptors are a family of ligand activated transcription factors involved in vertebrate development, behavior, and reproduction.
source: Steroid hormone receptors are a family of ligand activated transcription factors that are involved in vertebrate development, behavior, and reproduction (Bentley, 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge about steroid hormone receptors, supported by citation.

claim: There are two major subfamilies of steroid hormone receptors, which recognize distinct palindromic DNA response elements.
source: There are two major subfamilies of steroid hormone receptors, which recognize distinct palindromic DNA response elements (REs).
evidence: This is established knowledge about steroid hormone receptor classification.

claim: Estrogen receptors (ERs) bind to a palindrome of the ER response element (ERE, AGGTCA).
source: Estrogen receptors (ERs) bind to a palindrome of the ER response element (ERE, AGGTCA)
evidence: This is established knowledge about ER binding specificity.

claim: Ketosteroid receptors (kSRs) strongly prefer the steroid receptor response element (SRE, AGAACA).
source: whereas the ketosteroid receptors (kSRs, including the receptors for androgens, progestogens, glucocorticoids, and mineralocorticoids) strongly prefer the steroid receptor response element (SRE, AGAACA; Chusacultanachai et al., 1999; So et al., 2007; Welboren et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge about kSR binding specificity, supported by citations.

claim: The reconstructed DBD of AncSR1 was ERE-specific.
source: Earlier experiments showed that the reconstructed DBD of the last common ancestor of the two subfamilies (called AncSR1) was ERE-specific, whereas the last common ancestor of the kSRs (AncSR2) was SRE-specific (McKeown et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior experimental work.

claim: The reconstructed DBD of AncSR2 was SRE-specific.
source: Earlier experiments showed that the reconstructed DBD of the last common ancestor of the two subfamilies (called AncSR1) was ERE-specific, whereas the last common ancestor of the kSRs (AncSR2) was SRE-specific (McKeown et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior experimental work.

claim: Three substitutions in the recognition helix occurred during the interval between AncSR1 and AncSR2.
source: During the interval between AncSR1 and AncSR2, three substitutions occurred in the protein's recognition helix (RH), which inserts into the DNA major groove and makes contact with the bases that vary between ERE and SRE.
evidence: This is a historical inference from phylogenetic reconstruction.

claim: Three substitutions in the recognition helix were shown experimentally to cause the evolutionary change in specificity from ERE to SRE.
source: These substitutions were shown experimentally to cause the evolutionary change in specificity (McKeown et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior experimental work.

claim: The analyzed library contained all 160,000 combinations of 20 amino acids at four sites in the recognition helix.
source: The library contained all 160,000 combinations of 20 amino acids at four sites in the RH – the three historically substituted sites plus another site that is variable in closely related nuclear receptors.
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the DMS library.

claim: The library was transformed into yeast strains carrying either an ERE- or SRE-driven GFP reporter and functionally characterized using a FACS-based Sort-seq assay.
source: The library was transformed into yeast strains carrying either an ERE- or SRE-driven GFP reporter and functionally characterized using a FACS-based Sort-seq assay.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology.

claim: Categorization of variants into activation classes substantially reduced the effect of technical noise in the assay.
source: Categorization substantially reduced the effect of technical noise in the assay: concordance in the activation class assigned to each variant between replicates was >97%, much better than the between-replicate correlation of mean fluorescence as a continuous variable (R2=0.62 for functional variants, and R2=0.11 when null variants are included).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's data analysis comparing categorical and continuous measurements.

claim: Concordance in the activation class assigned to each variant between replicates was >97%.
source: concordance in the activation class assigned to each variant between replicates was >97%
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the study's data analysis.

claim: Across both REs, 1342 variants were classified as strong activators and 3166 as weak activators.
source: Across both REs, 1342 variants were classified as strong and 3166 as weak activators.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the study's data analysis.

claim: The ordinal regression model contains terms for the main effect of every possible amino acid at each variable site and for the epistatic effect of every pair and triplet of sites.
source: The model contains terms for the main effect of every possible amino acid at each variable site in the protein and for the epistatic effect of every pair and triplet of sites (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the structure of the model developed in the study, with reference to Figure 1A.

claim: The genetic score of each variant is defined as the sum of the main and epistatic effects of the sequence states and combinations it contains.
source: The genetic score of each variant is defined as the sum of the main and epistatic effects of the sequence states and combinations it contains (Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes how the model calculates genetic scores, with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: The model fits the experimental data well, with predicted class matching observed class for 99.5% of all variants.
source: When we used the best-fit model to predict the highest-probability activation class for each protein variant on each RE, the predicted class matched the observed class for 99.5% of all variants.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the model fitting procedure.

claim: The deviance of the model was 0.86.
source: The deviance of the model – an analog of the coefficient of determination used in linear regression – was 0.86 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the model fitting procedure.

claim: The genetic score of activators is well correlated with the apparent ΔG of dissociation from DNA (R2=0.75).
source: The genetic score of activators is well correlated with the apparent ΔG of dissociation from DNA, which was previously measured for a subset of variants by fluorescence anisotropy (R2=0.75, Figure 1—figure supplement 4
evidence: This is a quantitative result comparing model predictions to independent experimental measurements.

claim: Main effects and pairwise epistasis are important in RE recognition, but higher order epistasis is not.
source: We found that main effects and pairwise epistasis are important in RE recognition, but higher order epistasis is not.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the variance decomposition analysis.

claim: More than half of all genetic variance explained by the best-fit model is attributable to the main effects of single amino acids.
source: Of all the genetic variance explained by the best-fit model, more than half is attributable to the main effects of single amino acids
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the variance decomposition analysis.

claim: Main effects are the primary determinants of nonspecific DNA binding.
source: Main effects are the primary determinants of nonspecific DNA binding, but pairwise interactions explain the majority of RE-specificity.
evidence: This is a finding from the variance decomposition analysis.

claim: Pairwise interactions explain the majority of RE-specificity.
source: Main effects are the primary determinants of nonspecific DNA binding, but pairwise interactions explain the majority of RE-specificity.
evidence: This is a finding from the variance decomposition analysis.

claim: Third-order epistasis accounts for only 2% of total variance.
source: Third-order epistasis accounts for only 2% of total variance, with similarly small contributions to both nonspecific binding and specificity (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the variance decomposition analysis.

claim: The 99% set of model terms includes the main effect of every possible amino acid state at all four sites and >80% of all possible second-order epistatic terms.
source: This set includes the main effect of every possible amino acid state at all four sites and >80% of all possible second-order epistatic terms.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the variance decomposition analysis.

claim: The 99% set includes only 5% of all possible third-order terms.
source: By contrast, the 99% set includes only 5% of all possible third-order terms.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the variance decomposition analysis.

claim: Every amino acid state participates in a minimum of 60 pairwise interactions with states at other sites.
source: Every amino acid state participates in a minimum of 60 pairwise interactions with states at other sites (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of pairwise interactions.

claim: The most favorable effects on nonspecific binding come from having small-volume amino acids at site 2, particularly in combination with a basic residue at site 3.
source: The most favorable effects come from having small-volume amino acids at site 2, particularly in combination with a basic residue at site 3, which can potentially hydrogen-bond with a guanine common to both REs.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of main and pairwise effects, with structural rationalization.

claim: Small hydrophobic residues at site 4 favor SRE binding.
source: Small hydrophobic residues at site 4 favor SRE binding, where they can pack against the hydrophobic methyl groups that are unique to SRE but leave ERE's hydrogen bond (donors/acceptors) unpaired.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of specificity effects, with structural rationalization.

claim: Epistatic terms overwhelmingly enhance the function of active variants, contrary to the expectation of diminishing returns.
source: Contrary to the expectation of diminishing returns (in which epistasis predominantly impairs function; Chou et al., 2011; Tokuriki et al., 2012; Wei and Zhang, 2019; Wünsche et al., 2017), we found that epistatic terms overwhelmingly enhance the function of active variants.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the analysis of epistatic contributions to variant function.

claim: Epistatic terms make a net positive contribution to the genetic score of 100% of strong activators.
source: Epistatic terms make a net positive contribution to the genetic score of 100% of strong activators, contributing an average of 64% of the score needed to be a strong activator
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of epistatic contributions.

claim: The epistatic contribution was necessary to surpass the strong activator threshold in every single case.
source: and the epistatic contribution was necessary to surpass this threshold in every single case.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of epistatic contributions.

claim: Epistatic terms contribute positively to 98% of weak activators.
source: Weak activators also benefit from epistatic interactions, which contribute positively to 98% of variants in this class, but their effect is smaller.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of epistatic contributions.

claim: The number of strong activators in the main-effects-only model is reduced by about 25% compared to the third-order model.
source: Confirming the key role of epistasis in generating functional proteins, we found that the number of strong activators in the main-effects-only model is reduced by about 25% compared to the third-order model
evidence: This is a quantitative result from comparing models with and without epistasis.

claim: Of variants that are strong activators in the first-order model, only 64% remain strong activators when epistasis is included.
source: Epistasis also changes which sequences are functional: of variants that are strong activators in the first-order model, only 64% remain strong activators when epistasis is included.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from comparing models with and without epistasis.

claim: States with positive main effects on binding overwhelmingly have positive pairwise and third-order epistatic interactions.
source: Consistent with this explanation, states with positive main effects on binding overwhelmingly have positive pairwise and third-order epistatic interactions (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of epistatic interactions.

claim: There are >200,000 context-mutations that can transform a null protein into a functional activator.
source: We found that there are >200,000 context-mutations that can transform a null protein into a functional activator, and epistasis is critical to these transitions (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of mutation effects.

claim: 1160 of the 1520 unique types of amino acid exchanges move one or more variants into a higher activation class.
source: The underlying mutations are diverse, with 1160 of the 1520 unique types of amino acid exchanges moving one or more variants into a higher activation class (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of mutation effects.

claim: In 99% of cases where mutations promote variants to higher activation classes, the net epistatic impact of the mutation's effects are positive.
source: In nearly every case (99%), the net epistatic impact of the mutation's effects are positive
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of mutation effects.

claim: In 94% of cases where mutations promote variants to higher activation classes, the epistatic contribution is necessary to move the variant to the higher class.
source: in 94% of cases, the epistatic contribution is necessary to move the variant to the higher class
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of mutation effects.

claim: In almost half of cases where mutations promote variants to higher activation classes, epistasis is sufficient to move the variant to the higher class.
source: and in almost half of cases it is sufficient (Figure 4C–D).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of mutation effects.

claim: Every single one of the 1520 mutation types caused positive effects in some backgrounds and negative effects in others.
source: Sign epistasis was rampant among mutations: every single one of the 1520 mutation types caused positive effects in some backgrounds and negative effects in others
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of mutation effects across backgrounds.

claim: More than 90% of mutation types had both positive and negative effects on more than 10% of genetic backgrounds.
source: and more than 90% of mutation types (1380 of 1520) had both positive and negative effects on more than 10% of genetic backgrounds (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of mutation effects across backgrounds.

claim: There are hundreds of context-specific mutations and mutation types that change a strong ERE-specific activator directly into a strong SRE-specific activator.
source: There are hundreds of context-specific mutations and mutation types that change a strong ERE-specific activator directly into a strong SRE-specific activators.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of specificity-switching mutations.

claim: In every single case of specificity-switching mutations, the net change in epistatic effects caused by the mutation is necessary for the switch in specificity.
source: In every single case, the net change in epistatic effects caused by the mutation is necessary for the switch in specificity
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of specificity-switching mutations.

claim: In almost half of cases of specificity-switching mutations, the epistatic effects are also sufficient for the switch.
source: and in almost half of cases the epistatic effects are also sufficient (Figure 4G–H).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of specificity-switching mutations.

claim: Without epistasis, the total number of specificity-switching mutations is reduced by >80%.
source: Without epistasis, the total number of specificity-switching mutations is reduced by >80%, and the number of mutation types declines from 85 to just three (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from comparing models with and without epistasis.

claim: 99.8% of functional sequences are connected to each other in a single mutually accessible network given the best-fit third-order model.
source: Sign epistasis is generally thought to constrain epistasis by creating a fragmented sequence space in which local optima are separated by impassable valleys. Sign epistasis is rampant in our datasets (Figure 2D, Figure 4E), we found that given the best-fit third-order model, 99.8% of functional sequences are connected to each other in a single mutually accessible network (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the sequence space network analysis.

claim: The third-order model contains 1603 functional nodes, whereas the first-order epistasis-free model contains only 1080 functional nodes.
source: The third-order model contains 1603 functional nodes (1600 of which are connected in a single network), whereas the first-order epistasis-free model contains only 1080 functional nodes.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the sequence space network analysis.

claim: Including epistasis shortens the average path length to SRE-specificity for 80% of ERE-specific nodes.
source: In this scenario, including epistasis shortens the average path length to SRE-specificity for 80% of ERE-specific nodes, with an average reduction of 25% (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from evolutionary simulations.

claim: The minimum distance from ERE-specific starting points to the nearest SRE-specific variant is on average 10% shorter in the third-order model than in the first-order model.
source: First, the minimum distance from ERE-specific starting points to the nearest SRE-specific variant is on average 10% shorter in the third-order model than when epistasis is eliminated in the first-order model (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the sequence space network analysis.

claim: The average number of SRE-specific neighbors per ERE-specific node is 2.5 times higher in the third-order model than in the first-order model.
source: A second factor is that there are far more direct single-step mutations from ERE- to SRE-specific nodes: the average number of SRE-specific neighbors per ERE-specific node is 2.5 times higher in the third-order model
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the sequence space network analysis.

claim: In the third-order model, each ERE-specific node can reach its closest SRE-specific nodes by an average of 65 different paths.
source: Finally, epistasis increases the number of paths by which SRE specificity can evolve: in the third-order model, each ERE-specific node can reach its closest SRE-specific nodes by an average of 65 different paths
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the sequence space network analysis.

claim: Excluding epistasis shrinks the number of paths from ERE-specific to nearest SRE-specific nodes by about 20%.
source: excluding epistasis shrinks this number by about 20%, and these paths are less distinct (Figure 5G–H, Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the sequence space network analysis.

claim: Neither egKa nor GSKV is a strong activator on either RE under the main-effects only model.
source: Under the main-effects only model, neither egKa nor GSKV is a strong activator on either RE.
evidence: This is a result from applying the first-order model to historical sequences.

claim: Including the terms from the pairwise or third-order models restores the function of egKa and GSKV.
source: Including the terms from the pairwise or third-order models restores the function of these variants, because interactions make large and necessary contributions to their functions.
evidence: This is a result from applying higher-order models to historical sequences.

claim: The functionality of both historical and present-day steroid receptors depends critically on pairwise epistasis.
source: These RH sequences are conserved today in all known ERs and kSRs: therefore, the functionality of both historical and present-day steroid receptors depends critically on pairwise epistasis.
evidence: This is an inference from the model results applied to historical and extant sequences.

claim: The historical transition from ERE- to SRE-specificity altered the architecture by which REs are recognized, changing the sites and pairs that confer DNA binding.
source: The historical transition from ERE- to SRE-specificity also altered the architecture by which REs are recognized, changing the sites and pairs that confer DNA binding rather than just exchanging amino acid states within an otherwise fixed architecture (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of historical substitutions.

claim: The final substitution in the historical trajectory replaced the initial determinants of SRE specificity with a different set of favorable interactions.
source: Moreover, this architecture continued to change once the RH became SRE-specific: the final substitution in the trajectory (g2S, which had no net effect on specificity) replaced the initial historical determinants of SRE specificity with a different set of favorable interactions.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of historical substitutions.

claim: The final RH sequence has determinants of function that are entirely different from those in the ancestral RH and even those that first mediated the acquisition of SRE specificity during history.
source: As a result, the final RH sequence – which is now found in all extant kSRs – has determinants of function that are entirely different from those in the ancestral RH and even those that first mediated the acquisition of SRE specificity during history.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of historical substitutions.

claim: The study's findings differ from other studies because it takes a global instead of a local view of epistasis and expands the scope of analysis to incorporate all possible amino acid states for multiple functions.
source: These differences arise primarily because we take a global instead of a local view of epistasis, and we expand the scope of analysis to incorporate all possible amino acid states for multiple functions.
evidence: This is the authors' explanation for why their findings differ from prior work.

claim: Reference-based analyses provide an accurate local picture of mutation effects when introduced into the reference or nearby proteins, but accuracy is poor across other backgrounds.
source: This strategy provides an accurate local picture of mutation effects when they are introduced into the reference or nearby proteins, but accuracy is poor across other backgrounds and is very sensitive to experimental error (Poelwijk et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a characterization of limitations in reference-based methods, supported by citation.

claim: The study found only a small role for high-order epistasis, unlike most previous studies.
source: Like other researchers, we found pervasive epistasis within a protein (Buda et al., 2022; Otwinowski et al., 2018; Sailer and Harms, 2017a; Sailer and Harms, 2017b; Weinreich et al., 2018). Unlike most previous studies, we found that higher-order epistasis plays only a tiny role (Buda et al., 2022; Otwinowski et al., 2018; Sailer and Harms, 2017a; Sailer and Harms, 2017b; but see Weinreich et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a comparison of the study's findings to prior work, supported by citations.

claim: Prior work used reference-based methods and/or did not adequately account for global nonlinearities, which can cause spurious inference of higher order epistasis.
source: Why do our findings concerning higher order epistasis differ from previous studies? A likely cause is that prior work used reference-based methods and/or they did not adequately account for global nonlinearities. Both of these factors are known to cause spurious inference of higher order epistasis (Otwinowski et al., 2018; Poelwijk et al., 2019; Sailer and Harms, 2017b).
evidence: This is the authors' explanation for differences from prior work, supported by citations.

claim: The study found a dense genetic architecture at first and second orders, unlike some other studies that found a very sparse architecture.
source: Another difference from previous work is that we found a dense genetic architecture at first and second orders, such that main and pairwise effects involving virtually all possible states at all sites make substantial contributions to genetic architecture. Some other studies have found a very sparse architecture, with just a few states or combinations explaining the distribution of functions across variants (Poelwijk et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a comparison of the study's findings to prior work, supported by citation.

claim: One cause of the difference in density of genetic architecture may be that the study analyzed all 20 amino acid states rather than just two.
source: One cause of this difference may be that we analyzed all 20 amino acid states rather than just two, so the number of possible terms in our model is far larger than studies that analyze only pairs of states present in two high-functioning proteins.
evidence: This is the authors' speculation about causes of differences from prior work.

claim: Prior work has viewed epistasis as an evolutionary constraint, but this study found that the primary effect of epistasis is to facilitate functional evolution.
source: Prior work has viewed epistasis as an evolutionary constraint, but we found that the primary effect of epistasis is to facilitate functional evolution.
evidence: This is a comparison of the study's findings to prior work.

claim: Virtually all earlier studies on epistasis and evolution considered only the effect of epistasis on direct paths through a binary sequence space between two functional sequences designated a priori.
source: Virtually all earlier studies on this topic considered only the effect of epistasis on direct paths through a binary sequence space between two functional sequences designated a priori as starting and ending points, and they have focused on optimization of a single function.
evidence: This is a characterization of limitations in prior research.

claim: In the narrow perspective of prior work, the major effect of epistasis is to create idiosyncrasies in the functions of intermediates between two high-functioning proteins, so epistasis can only constrain evolution along those paths.
source: In that context, the major effect of epistasis is to create idiosyncrasies in the functions of the intermediates between two high-functioning proteins, so epistasis can only constrain evolution along those paths (Poelwijk et al., 2007; Weinreich et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a characterization of findings from prior research, supported by citations.

claim: Epistasis makes the topography of sequence space idiosyncratic enough that new functions are easily accessible from nodes with different functions, but not so idiosyncratic that functional nodes become inaccessible from each other.
source: Overall, epistasis makes the topography of sequence space idiosyncratic enough that new functions are easily accessible from nodes with different functions, but not so idiosyncratic that functional nodes become inaccessible from each other.
evidence: This is a synthesis of the study's findings about epistasis and evolution.

claim: The ordinal model approach could reduce precision in estimating genetic architecture compared to direct analysis of continuous phenotypic data.
